summary: work.py is largely correct on the COR dimension. The code-generation machinery (_make_calculate_code/_make_loader_code/_make_combine_code/_make_inputs_vector_code and the num_sources-keyed registries) is sound: the generated functions are type-generic over source types and only depend on the source count, the calculate/load/combine recursions correctly guard against diamond re-traversal (derived flag, harvested dict), and as_node/make_inputs_vector caching does not recurse or go stale. The only genuine defect found is a missing negative-index guard in get_input, which silently returns a wrong input instead of raising.

findings.title: get_input bounds check omits negative index
findings.claim: ol_get_input only rejects i >= num_inputs, not negative i. A negative argument (e.g. -1) is passed straight into the reflected-list-backed inputs_vector via inputs_vector[i], which performs Python-style negative-index wraparound and returns a different input than requested, silently producing a wrong result instead of raising the intended out-of-range error.
findings.evidence: ol_get_input body: `num_inputs = len(self.inputs); if i >= num_inputs: raise NumbaError(...); inputs_vector = self.make_inputs_vector(); return _cast(inputs_vector[i], NodeType)`. There is no `i < 0` check. inputs_vector is a `List.empty_list(NodeBaseType)` (see _make_inputs_vector_code, work.py:377-396), and numba typed/reflected lists honor negative indexing. node.py:81-88 ol_get_input has the identical gap, so the two are consistent, but both miss the lower bound.
findings.recommendation: Tighten the guard to `if i < 0 or i >= num_inputs:` in both ol_get_input bodies (work.py:356-364 and node.py:81-88) so an out-of-range request raises NumbaError rather than wrapping around.
